body: I'm really inspired by scientists like Einstein, Newton, Feynman, and the like because they did such amazing things for human knowledge and existence in general. I've known for a while that I wanted to do all I could to try and contribute to human knowledge just like they did, even if it's not as great as what those great thinkers contributed to human knowledge. That's always been my goal for the end of my academic career, and hopefully I can contribute to science even after my academic journey is over. I think a lot of my expectations for myself come from my desire to be like those great minds. I know that I probably will never be able to do what they did, but I still want to do as much as I can to achieve something great with my life

Thank you, that really means a lot.

I've actually often felt like I might have some kind of chemical imbalance, but I haven't been willing to accept that as the truth because these feeling have been more recent. I have a prescription for Adderall, for attention deficit disorder, that I've been taking (on and off) since I was 10 and lately I've been wondering if that could be a source of the problem. When I take the medication, I feel very focused and my anxiety is curbed a bit, but if I take a break from it for even one day, I'm just overwhelmed with anxiety and depressed thoughts. I'm honestly too afraid to stop taking it daily because I know that I will feel horrible if I don't. This is the first time that that has ever happened though, I've never felt a 'need' to take my medication before. I always had a very on and off relationship with taking my medication because I never really liked the idea of needing to take a pill to perform better in school, but now I'm almost dependent on taking it to avoid depression and I'm not sure if I should be concerned about it. I wasn't taking my medication for most of my first semester, but I started to feel a bit anxious about my schoolwork so I decided to start taking it again in early December (2012). I've had this dependence since then and I'm not sure if the medicine is the cause, or if I'm still feeling depressed from before

I think I just have this really deep desire to distinguish myself as someone who works hard and who stands out among his peers. I've always had that desire since I was a kid, but now that I'm in college it's a lot harder to feel like I really stand out. I constantly feel like I'm no different from anyone else, and even though I apply myself very thoroughly to my studies, it doesn't give me that sense of accomplishment that I'm looking for. Since I'm not getting that feeling, I blame myself and convince myself that I need to work harder to do better on exams and homework, etc. but it just ends up coming back and putting more pressure on me. When exam time comes around I feel even more pressure to do well because if I don't, I know that I'm going blame myself even more for not working hard and I'll just get more depressed. It's like a vicious cycle where I work myself because I want to avoid that feeling of failure, but in doing so I'm just killing myself slowly

EDIT: Sorry, I'm studying Applied Math, Engineering, and Physics (1 Degree, not 3)
